title: Plum and almond galette
subtitle: a free-form pastry tart with almond cream and halved plums, baked without a tin
excerpt: A plum and almond galette is a free-form shortcrust pastry round spread with almond cream, topped with halved plums, and baked on a flat tray. The edges are folded up loosely around the fruit rather than fitted into a tin, giving the finished galette a relaxed, rustic shape. It is quicker to make than a tart case and does not require blind baking.
sourceNotes: The galette is a French term for a free-form, flat pastry. Fruit galettes of this style, with a folded edge and no tin, appear widely in French home cooking and were popularised in British baking from the 1990s, particularly through writers such as Delia Smith and Nigel Slater.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The pastry can be made up to 2 days ahead and kept refrigerated. Assemble and bake the galette on the day.

content.text: A plum and almond galette is a free-form tart baked on a flat tray rather than in a tin. The pastry is rolled into a rough round, spread with a thin layer of almond cream, topped with halved plums, and the edges are folded up around the fruit. The fold does the job of a tart case: it holds the filling in and the shape comes from the pastry itself rather than a mould.

Make the pastry: rub the cold butter into the flour and sugar until the mixture looks like coarse breadcrumbs. Add cold water a tablespoon at a time, mixing lightly until the dough just comes together. Press into a flat disc, wrap, and chill for 30 minutes.
Make the almond cream: beat the softened butter and caster sugar until fluffy. Beat in the egg, then fold in the ground almonds.

Heat the oven to 190 degrees C (fan 170 degrees C / gas 5). Roll the chilled pastry on a lightly floured surface into a rough circle about 35 cm across and 3 mm thick. Transfer to a baking tray lined with baking paper.
Spread the almond cream over the pastry leaving a 5 cm border clear around the edge. Arrange the plum halves cut-side up over the almond cream, packing them fairly tightly as they will shrink.
Fold the pastry border up and over the edge of the fruit, pleating it every 5 cm and pressing gently to hold. Brush the folded edge with beaten egg and scatter with demerara sugar.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and the plums are soft and juicy. Cool on the tray for 20 minutes before serving.

attrs.problem: Pastry tears when folding the edge up around the fruit
attrs.avoid: Avoid rolling the pastry too thin or letting it warm up before assembly.
attrs.fix: Keep the pastry cold. If it tears, press it back together with your fingers. The galette is free-form; small imperfections in the edge are fine.

attrs.problem: Juices running onto the tray and burning
attrs.avoid: Avoid overfilling with very juicy plums without any buffer underneath.
attrs.fix: The almond cream absorbs some juice. Line the tray well with baking paper. If there is significant leakage, reduce the quantity of fruit slightly on the next batch.
